newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Capital Alliance set for JCI bid - paper.
newsitem.headline: Capital Alliance set for JCI bid - paper.

text.p: Black financial services group Capital Alliance has secured sufficient financing to buy a 35 percent shareholding in mining house JCI Ltd, Business Day newspaper reported on Friday.
The interest is worth 2.6 billion rand based on JCI's market capitalisation on Thursday.
However, the paper also quoted sources saying that a consortium including New African Investments Ltd (Nail) was preparing a rival bid.
Earlier this week Mark Barnes, formerly deputy managing director and head of treasury at Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank, resigned to become chief executive of Capital Alliance.
Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said earlier this week it expected talks on the sale of its majority shareholding in JCI to kick off soon.

Anglo, which holds 47 percent of JCI, said the sale of a stake of 35 percent would become a priority after the conclusion of the recent sale of control in conglomerate Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic) to black businesses.
JCI is South Africa's sixth-largest mining company and Anglo has said it wants to sell the company to black interests.

On Wednesday, Business Day newspaper reported that black empowerment group Real African Investments Ltd (Rail) had decided not to pursue a deal to buy the JCI stake, leaving the way open for rivals bidders.
